title: Gantt Studio
why: Mermaid turns a few lines of text into a tidy Gantt chart, but rescheduling it means retyping dates. Gantt Studio lets you drag the bars and writes the Mermaid back, keeping the fields Mermaid has no syntax for. A schedule you can review in a pull request: possible now, if not exactly requested.
gains: Handy for a small team planning without a project-management account. Dependencies push later tasks along by themselves, and a baseline shows how many days each task has drifted from the original plan: useful information, rarely good news.

flow.label: Drag from a bar's end dot

lessons: Dates stored at 00:00 UTC but read with local getters showed the day before anywhere west of UTC, and in Taipei "today" jumped to tomorrow at 20:00.
The scheduler gave up after 100 sweeps, so in big projects a chain stored backwards fell off the chart; it now walks the graph in topological order.
Exporting to Mermaid kept only each task's last predecessor, though Mermaid takes "after a b"; a round-trip test now expects the sample back unchanged.
subtitle: Plan visually. Edit as Mermaid.
description: Drag a schedule into place, draw dependencies and see the critical path. Switch to Mermaid text without losing the plan. Everything stays in your browser.
longDescription: A browser-only Gantt editor with visual scheduling and two-way Mermaid editing. Tasks, dependencies, baselines and working-day calendars live in localStorage. It needs no account or backend and exports PNG, Excel and JSON.
features: Drag tasks, resize durations and draw dependencies
Two-way Mermaid editing with metadata preserved
Automatic scheduling, critical path and baselines
Keyboard controls and four interface languages
